cocoa.black_pod: Black pod rot (Phytophthora). Remove and bury infected pods within 48h. Spray copper fungicide every 15 days in the rainy season. Prevention: prune, drain, harvest every 2 weeks and bury pod husks.
cocoa.mirids: Mirids (capsids): sap-sucking insects. Spray an approved insecticide in July-August, then October. Check young shoots every week. Prevention: managed shade.
cocoa.swollen_shoot: Suspected swollen shoot (CSSV virus, spread by mealybugs). No cure. Uproot and burn infected and neighbouring trees. Replant tolerant varieties. Alert the farm post.

littoral.label: Littoral
littoral.advice: No sun drying. Spray fungicide after 6pm if dry.

centre.label: Centre
centre.advice: Cocoa drying possible tomorrow morning. Spraying window 6am-10am.

west.label: West
west.advice: Good window for sowing and fertilising. Water the nurseries.

advice.answer: Cassava: spots or mosaic on leaves = likely mosaic disease or leaf spot. Uproot badly hit plants, use healthy cuttings of a tolerant variety, do not replant in the same spot. Ask the farm extension officer.
Cocoa: black pods = likely black pod rot. Remove sick pods, spray copper fungicide every 15 days in the rains, prune to let air through the farm.
Plantain: black streaks on leaves = likely black Sigatoka. Cut and burn infected leaves, space the plants, add organic matter. Avoid suckers from sick plants.
Maize: holes and frass in the whorl = likely fall armyworm. Inspect twice a week, hand-pick or apply an approved treatment early in the morning.
Tomato: brown spots and wilting = likely late blight. Remove infected leaves, do not wet the leaves when watering, spray copper fungicide and rotate crops.

defaultAdvice: General advice: isolate sick plants, do not replant in the same spot, use healthy seed. Send a photo to the farm extension officer of your district.
